source_text: Commendaveritque Apostolus transisse peccatum, sed per unum, ostenderitque hoc veritas ad exemplum proprie pertinere, intolerabili impudentia Traducianus facit, ut dicat et ad se illum numerum inflexum abusione pertingere.
pass_a_gloss: And the Apostle has commended that sin passed, but through one, and truth has shown that this properly pertains to an example—the advocate of inherited sin does with intolerable shamelessness that he say that that number, bent by abuse, extends also to him.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: And the apostle has emphasized that sin passed, but through one, while truth has shown that this properly refers to an example—the advocate of inherited sin acts with intolerable shamelessness when he says that the number, bent into an inexact sense, can extend to his position too.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Repeats or discusses sin entering or passing through one man.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
